description:
Give `jmap-tasks-types` callers typed access to the 13 sloppy-Value fields whose wire shapes are RFC 8984 JSCalendar sub-types, by consuming the new `jmap-jscalendar-types` crate (extracted under the parallel epic).

## Strategy decision (resolved 2026-05-10)

The original epic offered three strategies. The decision is **Strategy 3 (extract to a new shared crate)**. See the parallel extraction epic for the full rationale.

Summary:
- Option 1 (duplicate jscalendar.rs as jstask.rs) — rejected: 559 lines duplicated, errata require parallel patches, weakens cookie-cutter pattern.
- Option 2 (jmap-tasks-types depends on jmap-calendars-types) — rejected: spec-inverted dependency. Tasks and Calendars are parallel JMAP capabilities, neither depends on the other in the spec.
- **Option 3 (extract to new jmap-jscalendar-types crate) — chosen**: spec-aligned, single source of truth, pre-publish window keeps the breaking-API cost at zero.

After Strategy 3 lands (via the extraction epic), this epic shrinks dramatically. Almost all the work moves to the extraction epic; what's left here is: add a path-dep, write the consumer-side tests, document the pattern.

## Scope (post-strategy-resolution)

In scope:
- Add `jmap-jscalendar-types = { path = "../crate-jmap-jscalendar-types" }` to `crate-jmap-tasks-types/Cargo.toml`.
- Optional re-export: `pub use jmap_jscalendar_types::*;` (or selective list) in `crate-jmap-tasks-types/src/lib.rs` so callers can do `jmap_tasks_types::Location` symmetrically with `jmap_calendars_types::Location`. Recommend the re-export for symmetry with calendars-types.
- Round-trip tests for each of the 13 sloppy fields against RFC 8984 example JSON, demonstrating `serde_json::from_value::<jmap_jscalendar_types::Location>(task.locations.unwrap())` etc.
- Update `crate-jmap-tasks-types/PLAN.md` "JSCalendar complex sub-objects are serde_json::Value" section: replace "a future crate provides typed JSCalendar types" with "JSCalendar typed sub-types are available via the `jmap-jscalendar-types` crate, re-exported here for symmetry with `jmap-calendars-types`."

Out of scope:
- Changing the public Task / TaskList / TaskNotification structs or their Sloppy-Value fields (those stay as the wire-format anchor per workspace policy).
- Changing the JMAP wire format.
- Creating new typed sub-types (that work is done in jmap-jscalendar-types via the extraction epic).

## Sloppy fields newly accessible as typed sub-types

After this epic, callers of jmap-tasks-types can use `serde_json::from_value` to obtain typed views of:

Task (src/task.rs): related_to, locations, virtual_locations, links, recurrence_rules, excluded_recurrence_rules, recurrence_overrides, participants, alerts, localizations, time_zones (11 fields).
TaskList (src/task_list.rs): default_alerts_with_time, default_alerts_without_time (2 fields).

The wire-format storage stays as `Option<serde_json::Value>` per workspace policy; typed access is opt-in via `from_value`.

## Acceptance criteria

- `jmap-tasks-types` has a path-dep on `jmap-jscalendar-types`.
- Optional but recommended: top-level re-export so `jmap_tasks_types::Location` and `jmap_calendars_types::Location` both work, mirroring the cookie-cutter symmetry between the two crates.
- `crate-jmap-tasks-types/PLAN.md` updated to remove the "future crate" wording and document the actual consumer pattern.
- Round-trip tests added for each of the 13 sloppy fields using RFC 8984 example JSON. Tests use independent oracle (hand-written from RFC examples), NOT derived from the code under test.
- `cargo doc -p jmap-tasks-types --all-features --no-deps` clean.
- `cargo clippy -p jmap-tasks-types --tests -- -D warnings` clean.
- `cargo test -p jmap-tasks-types --all-features` clean.

## Decomposition

Trivial after Strategy 3 lands — likely a single PR. Possible split if needed:
- .1: Add path-dep, re-export, update PLAN.md.
- .2: Add round-trip tests against RFC 8984 examples (13 fields).

But .1 + .2 are small enough to land in one bead.

## Dependency

This epic is **blocked by the jmap-jscalendar-types extraction epic**. Cannot start until the new crate exists.

## Source material

- crate-jmap-jscalendar-types (after extraction epic lands) — the typed sub-types.
- crate-jmap-tasks-types/PLAN.md — current sloppy-Value rationale, needs update.
- RFC 8984 (JSCalendar) full text: ~/PROJECT/jmap-chat-spec/references/rfc8984.txt — test-vector source.

## Companion epic

JMAP-sehw is the parallel epic for jmap-contacts-types. Its strategy is being updated 2026-05-10 to mirror this one: extract typed RFC 9553 sub-types to a new `jmap-jscontact-types` crate from the start (since the types don't exist yet, this is "create" not "extract", but the crate-boundary shape is the same).
notes: 2026-05-09: BLOCKS JMAP-lbdy (extras-preservation policy epic). Per Mark's decision, this epic lands BEFORE JMAP-lbdy so the new typed sub-types get the extras policy applied in one sweep rather than retroactively. When implementing this epic's typed sub-types, do NOT pre-emptively add the extras pattern — leave that to JMAP-lbdy.6 which will sweep across after this lands.
title: EPIC: jmap-tasks-types consumes jmap-jscalendar-types (Strategy 3 resolved)
